entries.proposition: The review dates the epilepsy-ferroptosis link to a single kainic acid rat study and states the field is at an initial stage.
entries.snippet: Since the first study to report that ferroptosis was involved in seizure-induced cell death in rats and the associated cognitive comorbidities of kainic acid (KA)-induced temporal lobe epilepsy (Ye et al., 2019)

entries.proposition: The only human data point cited in the body: haematological findings in children with epilepsy (raised 4-HNE and NOX2, depleted GSH, inactivated GPX4); a cited result, no cohort detail in this review.
entries.snippet: Previous indications that ferroptosis is involved in epilepsy were substantiated by hematological findings in children with epilepsy, which showed a consistent increase in 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) and NAPDH oxidase 2 (NOX2), depletion of GSH, and inactivation of GPX4 (Petrillo et al., 2021).
entries.anchor: 3.1 The role of ferroptosis in epilepsy-associated neuronal death

entries.proposition: Ferroptosis in a mitochondrial-disease epilepsy context: EPI-743 reduced lipid peroxidation in cells from patients with five distinct paediatric epilepsy syndromes (a cited cell study).
entries.snippet: Another report demonstrated the role of ferroptosis in the pathogenesis of mitochondrial disease-associated epilepsies and found that α-tocotrienol quinone (EPI-743) potently dose-dependently ameliorated ferroptosis in the cells of patient of five distinct pediatric epilepsy syndromes by reducing LPO and 15-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (15-HETE), a specific 15-LO product (Kahn-Kirby et al., 2019).
entries.anchor: 4 Pharmacological inhibition of ferroptosis to treat epilepsy

entries.proposition: Astrocyte route: A1 astrocytes were reported to induce neuronal ferroptosis through CXCL10/CXCR3 in PTZ-kindled mice (cited result).
entries.snippet: A recent study revealed a correlation between astrocytic activation and neuronal ferroptosis in C57BL/6J male mice models of PTZ kindling-induced epileptic seizures and showed that A1 astrocytes induce ferroptosis via the chemokine receptor CXCL10/CXCR3 axis in epilepsy (Liang et al., 2023).
entries.anchor: 3.2 The role of astrocyte activation-induced neuronal ferroptosis in epilepsy

entries.proposition: Iron is described as a requirement for myelination and brain iron enters through transferrin/TfR1 at brain microvascular endothelium; iron handling is thus linked to the blood-brain barrier in the review's mechanism section.
entries.snippet: As an essential redox-active metal for neuronal activity and normal physiological function, iron plays a vital role in energy metabolism, biosynthesis, neurotransmission, and myelination (Crichton et al., 2011).

entries.proposition: The conclusion names oligodendrocyte, astrocyte and microglial involvement in ferroptosis as undetermined.
entries.snippet: Third, although neuron-glia interactions have a clear role in the pathophysiology of epilepsy, whether other cells, such as oligodendrocytes, astrocytes, and microglia, are involved in modulating ferroptosis has yet to be determined.

entries.proposition: The conclusion calls ferrostatin an iron chelator causing systemic iron deprivation, while Table 1 lists ferrostatin-1 under GPX4 and P38 MAPK modes of action; the review does not reconcile the two statements.
entries.snippet: However, the potential drawbacks or limitations of the proposed pharmacological interventions such as ferrostatin as iron chelator causing systemic iron deprivation and thew role of multidrug resistance transporter P-glycoproteins that limit drug efficacy is uncertain

entries.proposition: Table 1 models are chemically or traumatically induced seizures in mice and rats, or cell-line stress (glutamate, erastin, ferric ammonium citrate); the epilepsy-type column lists temporal lobe, posttraumatic and generalized clonic-tonic types, none genetic.
